newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Rumoured suitors deny Karstadt talk.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Rumoured suitors deny Karstadt talk.

text.p: Two rumoured suitors for Karstadt AG, whose shares have surged more than 100 marks this week on takeover speculation, denied on Thursday they were interested in taking a stake in the German retailer.

Germany's holding group WCM AG and Dutch supermarket group Ahold NV both said they were not interested in the retailer, whose shares again surged on Thursday to end bourse trade up 31 marks at 694 marks.
WCM management board member Guenter Vollman told Reuters the renewed market rumours about Karstadt were unfounded.
"There's nothing to the talk of us taking a stake in Karstadt," Vollman said. "The shares are so expensive that WCM does not have any more interest. There are no discussions at the moment."

WCM had said in mid-June that it was no longer interested in buying a 25 percent in Karstadt. WCM top shareholder Karl Ehlerding told the Handelsblatt daily newspaper on June 18 that "we have put acquiring a stake in Karstadt behind us".
WCM had indeed expressed an interest in buying stakes of 10 percent each in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG but pulled out after finding the banks' asking price too high.
Ahold also reaffirmed on Thursday that it had no immediate ambitions in the German market in response to a Reuter inquiry. The group in May had issued a similar statement to the rumours.

Some dealers said the extensive gains are particularly puzzling since Karstadt is very likely to be removed from the 30-share DAX index at a German bourse meeting on July 22 and replaced by sportswear group Adidas AG.
Top blue-chip companies that were removed in the past from the DAX index, which takes effect in September, have seen their shares tumble as institutional investors reshuffle portfolios.

But one confirmed fact seen supportive for Karstadt is the success of a pilot project at a store in Duisburg where the clothing department was remodelled as part of a new "theme" idea to revamp entire stores. The test has seen double-digit sales growth in the clothing unit on a same-space basis.
Analysts are hoping a broad-based expansion of the project over the next three years will help revive Karstadt, which saw a 2.3 percent drop in first quarter sales to 5.9 billion marks.
But the project is not seen as warranting such hefty gains.
One Frankfurt analyst called the nearly 20 percent rise since last Friday's bourse close at 610 marks "a grotesque overreaction" to market rumours.

"Rumours are popping up every day but this price reaction in Karstadt is well overdone," said Joerg Christians at Trinkaus Capital Markets in Duesseldorf, who rates the Essen-based retailer as a "sell" and time to take profits.
A Karstadt spokesman declined comment on the rumour.
"The rumour mill around Karstadt will not stop," said Thomas Teetz, analyst at Bankgesellschaft Berlin. "The talk is still that Karstadt is a potential takeover candidate."

The market is also picking over rumours that Karstadt may be transformed into a holding group and that its units - department store group Karstadt, mail-order group Neckermann and travel group NUR -- would be listed as individual shares.
Analysts have put little credence in such a plan.
Calls for Karstadt Chief Executive Walter Deuss, in power since 1979, to resign have also caused its shares to waver. But Deuss has shown no sign of stepping down from power.
